hero.eyebrow: Free and open source · on your own computer
hero.sub: A desktop studio for your brand's posts, ads and short videos. Set the brand once as patterns, then fill them yourself or let your AI model do it, and knit every size in one go.
hero.caption: The studio today, with a FileFreak post open and its patterns beside it.

idea.title: Pattern once. Knit forever.
idea.lead: Lock what the brand decided. Leave the rest free. Then change one line and watch every size follow. This is a small, working model of it.

items.title: Set your brand
items.text: Give it your website. knitted reads your colours, fonts and logo into a Swatch, and pictures of every page into the Brief.
items.alt: The Swatch of a project: its colours, fonts and logo

items.title: Build patterns
items.text: Lay out a post, a story or an ad once. Lock what the brand decided; leave the headline and the photo free.
items.alt: The pattern editor, with a post on the canvas, its layers on the left and its settings on the right

items.title: Knit every size
items.text: Fill the free slots, press Knit, and get PNG, JPEG or MP4 in every size, sorted into folders.
items.alt: A folder of knitted posts in the studio

model.title: Watch it work. Pause it any time.
model.text: Connect Claude Code, or add your Anthropic key and ask inside the app. Your model reads the brand, fills patterns, designs pages and knits, on the same canvas you use. What it changes is outlined in red with its name, and Pause holds its changes until you say so.
ticks: Follow it from screen to screen
Pin a comment to a spot and it does what it says
Locked stitches stay locked, for it too
model.alt: The studio while a model files knits into a folder: the folder and each knit are outlined in red, with what the model is doing

lock.title: Your brand stays put.
lock.text: Most tools drift. A model gets a little creative with the logo, someone nudges the red, and by Friday nothing matches. In knitted a locked stitch is locked for everyone, your model included. If it tries, the write is refused and the refusal is reported back, so nobody believes a change happened when it did not.

motion.title: Built frame by frame.
motion.text: A video is not a pile of pictures pasted on a timer. Each frame of a knitted animation is made at an exact moment, so things ease, fade and slide the way they do on a good website. Then it is encoded, and the result is the same on a slow laptop as on a fast one.
motion.voice: Voiceover is made by a speech model running on your own computer. Everything runs on your computer.

gallery.title: Real knits, from one set of patterns.
gallery.note: Each of these came out of the studio as it is today, for FileFreak, a file-hosting brand.

items.alt: Post: Surprise bill? Not here. The FileFreak mascot surrounded by flames.
Post: 5 GB free, with no card, beside the mascot.
Post: Go back a deploy in one command, with a terminal.
Ad: Ship from one place, beside the mascot.
Post: Ship a site from your terminal.
Post: Links that know when to stop.

sheets.title: Whole sites, on one board.
sheets.text: Foundations, components and every page on a computer and a phone, drawn from your Swatch, in labelled sections like a Figma file. Design them yourself or with your model, comment on any frame, and download them with a style guide.
sheets.alt: A design sheet in the studio: a website's colours, type, components and pages on one board

items.title: Runs offline
items.text: Fonts, tools and renderer all live on your machine. No account, no cloud, no tracking.

items.title: Your files, your folder
items.text: Projects are plain files in a folder you can open, copy and back up.

items.title: MIT licensed
items.text: Read it, change it, keep it. Free for you and for anyone who wants to build on it.

final.title: Knit your first post tonight.
final.text: The desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux is not released yet. Star the project and you will see it the moment it is.
final.released: Download the studio, give it your website, and your first patterns are ready to fill. Free, for Windows, macOS and Linux.
